stem: Tool arguments are untrusted input because…
options: They are assembled by a text predictor that may be conditioned on attacker-written text, and the loop retries
explanation: Validate as if they came from the internet - indirectly they did.

options: Schema (shape), reality (the world's bounds), policy (caps and rules) — none optional
explanation: Defence in depth: the naive tool died for lacking all three.

options: Consequential tools stage a proposal; execution is a separate code path requiring real identity
explanation: The model's schema has no execute in it - like CI not pushing to prod.

options: Check the arguments against the world: the order exists, the amount is within what is refundable
explanation: Shape says number; reality says ≤ 50.00 refundable on this order.

stem: Tools must be idempotent by key because…
options: The loop retries (5.1, 7.2), so any non-idempotent action can happen twice
explanation: One refund per order per reason; the retry is a no-op.

stem: The naive refund tool's failure was that it…
options: 'Worked' on every call — paying out on an eval'd expression, a nonsense id and a negative amount
explanation: No jailbreak needed; plausible text was enough.

stem: The defence against a search tool queried for another customer's data is…
options: The tool's own authorisation: it searches only what the current user may see, regardless of query text
explanation: Tools carry the caller's real permissions, never the model's ambitions.

stem: Tool names and descriptions deserve care because…
options: They are the only documentation the model gets - they decide when and how it calls
explanation: Vague contracts produce vague calls, forever.

stem: Tool errors return as data (not exceptions) because…
options: The model can recover from 'not found'; it cannot recover from an exception in your process

stem: Every tool call is audited so that…
options: The agent's actions are reconstructable from the trace — for debugging, evals and incident review
